chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: The fine dispute with Cab and Mister Wright
summary: Danny recounts borrowing thirty dollars, asking Cab why only he was fined, and handing in his notice.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: We did the big ones and the small ones. We'd go out there... I just want to say this. You see, what...
So Mister Wright says, "You know, Cab Calloway fined you." I asked him, said, "Give me a loan," so he gives me, I think, thirty dollars. So I am getting a hundred and a

quarter. He said, "Now, you know you're fined, so don't (?) yourself." I said, "Fined? Did you fine anybody else?" He said, "No, he didn't fine nobody else." But payday comes, and I got my money, and I was twenty dollars out. I said, "Cab, why did you fine me and you didn't fine the rest of them guys that was late?" He said, "Well, you know better." I said, "I know better? Well, okay. I'm gonna quit the band." He says, "Oh, man. Go on and ...(??)... Go and work. Don't come at me with that kind of shit, that talk."

So I walked out and I went and wrote a notice, and I give it to Mister Wright." So Cab calls me, and says, "Man, why did you quit? What did I do to you?" I said, "You fined me." He said, "Well, you know better." I said, "Well, just give me my twenty dollars." Because if they fine you, they got to pay you. They can't take your money. If you stay, you're subject to the...
